Thanks Markus — and appreciate the quick recap. A few quick answers from our security intake side: 

- SOC 2: we require SOC 2 Type II evidence for vendors in our production path. Veridian has an intake window of ~2 weeks to review reports (NDA-first).
- HIPAA: yes, we’ll need clarifying language on PHI handling and Business Associate Agreement (BAA) terms; our legal team will share a sample.
- HSM: for keys that encrypt PHI at-rest we prefer HSM-backed keys with FIPS 140-2 Level 3 if possible. For PoC we can accept HSM-backed KMS in customer tenant (BYOK) rather than on-prem HSM, but will validate for production.
- Questionnaire: please send an Excel or a shared Drive spreadsheet, that’s easiest for our GRC team.

Attaching our PoC requirements matrix for context — see the section on key custody and retention. Also looping in Tom from our security engineering group to coordinate the tech touchpoints.

Attachments: veridian_poc_requirements.xlsx

Best,
Sarah Jenkins

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Hi Sarah / Tom — thanks for the clarity and for the PoC matrix. Below are concise technical answers and where you can find the artifacts; I’ll also attach a short evidence pack separately once we have an NDA in place.

Encryption:
- At-rest: all customer data at rest is encrypted with AES-256-GCM. For object stores and disk volumes we use provider-managed encryption keys by default, but customers can choose customer-managed keys.
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 (strong ciphers only) for all external/internal RPCs and S3-compatible traffic; mTLS available for private deployments.

Customer-managed keys / BYOK options:
- Hosted BYOK: customer can supply a CMK in their cloud (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and Redwood will use that CMK for envelope encryption. Keys are HSM-backed when customer selects that option (e.g., AWS KMS with KMS keys backed by HSM).
- Importable keys: for customers that require key material import we support AWS KMS imported key material and Azure Key Vault import flows (subject to cloud provider policies).
- On-prem / dedicated HSM: for Private deployments we can integrate with customer PKCS#11 HSMs (YubiHSM/HSM vendors) and run with keys that never leave the HSM.

Key lifecycle & controls:
- Rotation: customer-managed rotation schedule (we can trigger and coordinate rotation; we also support automatic envelope key rotation at configurable intervals).
- Revocation: keys can be disabled/revoked in the customer KMS; Redwood will stop being able to decrypt new tokens following revocation (we advise a planned rotation strategy for smooth cutover).
- Dual control / split-auth: supported via customer KMS policies and role separation; for on-prem HSMs we recommend dual-control via HSM vendor tooling (unseal workflows).

Auditing & evidence:
- Audit logs: we produce per-request logs with key usage metadata (timestamp, request id, model id, key id). Logs are retained per contract and can be streamed to customer SIEM or delivered via secure link for audits.
- SOC 2 artifacts: our SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA; expected next refresh Q1 2028.

FIPS & certs:
- FIPS 140-2: when customers select cloud-provider HSM-backed CMKs, the HSM attestation is inherited from the provider (e.g., AWS CloudHSM). For on-prem HSM we support vendor attestation documents for your review.

Next steps proposed: 
1) We can share a minimal vendor questionnaire template (Excel) and a mapping document to our controls.
2) If helpful, schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with our infra/security engineer to walk through architecture and the PoC matrix items.
3) Share NDA and then we’ll attach SOC 2 artifacts and the control mapping.

I can run the deep-dive this week Thursday or next Monday. Let me know what works for Veridian.

— Markus
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
